findings.summary: Global monkey-patch of the third-party `CodeMirror.commands` singleton from an engine `initialize()`
findings.evidence: `routeVimHistoryToStore()` mutates `CodeMirror.commands.undo/redo` on the `@replit/codemirror-vim` module object, process-wide, the first time any note editor mounts (`initialize()` line 137 calls it). The store is resolved from the view facet so non-note editors fall through, but this is still a permanent module-level side effect owned by a package rather than an editor extension — the repo's other undo migrations (Slides/Docs) needed no equivalent global patch. A view-local vim `Vim.defineAction`/keymap override, or a `Prec.high` keymap in the vim compartment, would keep the effect scoped to the mount. The comment concedes "editors that are not notes (none today)" — i.e. the safety rests on there being no second consumer.

findings.summary: Vim `:undo` / `:redo` ex-commands are left silently inert by disabling CodeMirror history
findings.evidence: The engine disables `basicSetup`'s `history` and routes only `CodeMirror.commands.undo/redo`. Both the code comment and docs/design/notes/notes.md:300 state that vim's `:undo`/`:redo` ex-commands snapshot the original handlers at module load and "are inert". In vim keymap mode a user typing `:undo` now gets a silent no-op where P1 undid an edit. The issue's task list only names Cmd+Z / Cmd+Shift+Z, so this is a taste/completeness gap rather than a failed acceptance criterion, but shipping a known silently-dead command with no fallback (e.g. re-defining the ex-command via `Vim.defineEx`) is worth deciding explicitly.

findings.summary: Undo granularity regression (per-transaction instead of time-grouped) accepted with no mitigation for a prose editor
findings.evidence: The doc notes "CodeMirror grouped keystrokes into a time window (`newGroupDelay`), while Yorkie's unit is the change — so undo now steps per CodeMirror transaction", i.e. per keystroke in a markdown *text* editor. Docs/Slides tolerate this because their edit units are coarser (block/element ops); a note is free-form typing, so a user who types a sentence must now press Cmd+Z once per character. `note-sync` already owns the batching boundary (one ViewUpdate = one batch), so a time/idle-window coalescing of consecutive input transactions into one batch would be the natural place to preserve the old feel. findings.summary: Undo floor captured once at construction can strand undo permanently if Yorkie resets the undo stack afterwards
findings.evidence: `undoFloor = doc.getUndoStackForTest().length` is read in the constructor and `canUndo()` requires `getUndoStackForTest().length > this.undoFloor`. findings.summary: MemNoteStore undo/redo emits a whole-document `replace`, which resets the caret to the end of the document
findings.evidence: `undo()`/`redo()` call `this.emit({ type: 'replace', content: this.text })`; `noteSync.applyRemote` turns a `replace` into `changes: { from: 0, to: doc.length, insert: content }` (note-sync.ts:33-37). CodeMirror maps a cursor inside a fully replaced range to the end of the inserted text, so every undo/redo in the non-Yorkie store jumps the caret to the end of the note and discards any selection, instead of leaving it near the reverted edit (the Yorkie store, which emits per-op `edits`, does not have this problem). findings.summary: A throw inside the batched `doc.update` now discards every edit of the ViewUpdate while CodeMirror keeps them, desyncing view and model
findings.evidence: All `store.editText` calls for one ViewUpdate now run inside a single `YorkieNoteStore.batch()`, i.e. one `doc.update`. Yorkie rolls the whole update back and rethrows when the callback throws (e.g. `root.content.edit` on a document whose `content` is missing or was persisted as a plain object — the case `ensureText` in notes-view.tsx:42 exists to repair, and which is skipped entirely on read-only mounts). Previously each `editText` was its own `doc.update`, so a failure lost one edit; now a single failure silently drops every change carried by that transaction while the CodeMirror document keeps all of them, and CodeMirror catches the exception out of the plugin's `update()` and disables the plugin, so sync stops entirely from that point.

findings.summary: `MemNoteStore` keeps unbounded full-text snapshot stacks, so note content accumulates in memory with no cap and is retained after being deleted from the document.

Fix belongs on the new code: only open the batch when the update actually contains a non-remote, user-event transaction.

findings.evidence: `undoFloor` is captured once in the constructor (yorkie-note-store.ts:49) and never re-captured. The sibling stores expose an explicit re-base for this class of problem — `YorkieSlidesStore.markUndoBaseline()` (packages/frontend/src/app/slides/yorkie-slides-store.ts:669) and `YorkieDocStore.setDocument` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:732) — and `notes-view.tsx` only builds the store once per `doc` (useEffect deps `[didMount, doc]`, notes-view.tsx:108), so nothing rebuilds it after a snapshot. Confirming needs the @yorkie-js/sdk snapshot path (does `applySnapshot` clear history?), which is not installed in this worktree.

findings.evidence: `basicSetup({ history: false, historyKeymap: false })` (editor.ts:279-283) removes the history extension that `@codemirror/commands`' `undo/redo` need, and `routeVimHistoryToStore()` only re-points `CodeMirror.commands.undo/redo`. The branch's own design doc records the consequence for the out-of-diff vim path: "Its `:undo` / `:redo` ex-commands snapshot the original handlers at module load and cannot be re-routed; they are inert." (docs/design/notes/notes.md:300-302). Vim-mode users who type `:undo` previously got a working undo and now get nothing, with no feedback.

findings.summary: Toolbar undo/redo enablement still derives from the view's selection callback, which is no longer the source of truth for store-owned history

+# Notes native undo — migrate to Yorkie `doc.history` (issue #604)
+
+PR: (to be filled after opening)
+
+## Goal
+
+Move WaffleNotes undo/redo off CodeMirror's local history onto
+Yorkie-native undo (`doc.history`), so undo carries CRDT semantics and
+preserves a peer's concurrent edits instead of last-write-wins-ing over
+them. Reuses the pattern already shipped in Slides
+(`docs/design/slides/slides-native-undo.md`) and Docs
+(`packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts`).
+
+## Prerequisite spike (done — result recorded here)
+
+Verified against the pinned `@yorkie-js/sdk` 0.7.13 that character-level
+`Text.edit()` **is** reversible through `doc.history`:
+
+- Two `content.edit()` calls inside ONE `doc.update()` push exactly one
+  undo-stack entry; `history.undo()` reverts both, `redo()` re-applies.
+- The undo emits a `local-change` event with `source === 'undoredo'`
+  carrying `edit` ops on `$.content` with correct `from`/`to`/`content`
+  (already reversed in apply order), i.e. the dormant `isUndoRedo` path
+  in `yorkie-note-store.ts` receives exactly what it needs.
+- A `doc.update()` whose body mutates nothing pushes **no** undo entry,
+  so an empty batch is free.
+
+(`Tree.editByPath` merge non-reversibility, called out in the issue,
+does not apply — notes store markdown in a single `Text`.)
+
+## Approach
+
+**Store layer (`packages/notes/src/store/store.ts`)** — extend
+`NoteStore` with `batch(fn)`, `undo()`, `redo()`, `canUndo()`,
+`canRedo()`. Undo becomes store-owned (like `DocStore`/`SlidesStore`)
+rather than view-owned.
+
+**`YorkieNoteStore`** — ambient-root + `withUpdate()`: a top-level
+`batch()` opens ONE `doc.update()` and every `editText()` runs against
+that ambient root, so one CodeMirror transaction group = one Yorkie
+change = one undo unit. `setLocalSelection` folds into the batch's
+ambient presence proxy when a batch is open. `undo()/redo()` delegate to
+`doc.history`, gated by an undo floor captured at construction (after
+`ensureText()` seeding) so a user cannot undo the seed away.
+
+**`MemNoteStore`** — snapshot-based local history so the engine still
+has working undo without a CRDT (tests / non-collaborative use). Undo
+emits a `replace` remote change so the view reflects it, mirroring how
+the Yorkie store's undo comes back through `subscribeRemote`.
+
+**`note-sync.ts`** — wrap the per-`ViewUpdate` `editText` loop in
+`store.batch()`.
+
+**`editor.ts`** — `basicSetup({ history: false, historyKeymap: false })`;
+bind `Mod-z` / `Mod-Shift-z` / `Mod-y` to the store (skipped in
+read-only); `NoteEditorAPI.undo/redo/canUndo/canRedo` delegate to the
+store. Vim's `u` / `<C-r>` go through `CodeMirror.commands.undo/redo`,
+which the vim adapter looks up at call time — override them once to
+route to the note store resolved from the view's `noteStoreFacet`, else
+vim undo would silently no-op with CM history disabled.
+
+## Tasks
+
+- [ ] `NoteStore`: `batch` / `undo` / `redo` / `canUndo` / `canRedo`
+- [ ] `MemNoteStore`: snapshot history + `replace` emission on undo/redo
+- [ ] `YorkieNoteStore`: ambient root, `withUpdate`, batch, undo floor,
+      `doc.history` delegation
+- [ ] `note-sync.ts`: wrap local edits in `store.batch()`
+- [ ] `editor.ts`: disable CM history, history keymap → store, API
+      delegation, vim command routing
+- [ ] Tests: batch grouping = 1 undo unit, undo floor, peer-edit
+      preservation (churn regression), no-echo on undo, MemNoteStore
+      history, engine-level keybinding
+- [ ] `docs/design/notes/notes.md`: Yorkie-native undo section
+
+## Out of scope
+
+- Time-based keystroke coalescing (Yorkie's undo unit is the change;
+  Docs and Slides behave the same way).
+- `:undo` / `:redo` ex-commands in vim (the vim package snapshots those
+  handlers at module load, so they cannot be re-routed).

samples.summary: MemNoteStore undo/redo emits a whole-document `replace`, which resets the caret to the end of the document

samples.summary: A throw inside the batched `doc.update` now discards every edit of the ViewUpdate while CodeMirror keeps them, desyncing view and model
samples.evidence: All `store.editText` calls for one ViewUpdate now run inside a single `YorkieNoteStore.batch()`, i.e. one `doc.update`.
